concept_name: Power in AC Circuits — The Power Factor
source_book:
NCERT Class 12 Physics, Ch.7 Alternating Current, §7.7 Power in AC Circuit: The Power Factor — table-of-contents reference only; teaching authored from first principles, no sequence/example/figure imported. Sixth of 8 in the founder-reordered Ch.7 map (ac_voltage_resistor -> ac_voltage_inductor -> ac_voltage_capacitor -> phasors -> series_lcr_circuit -> ac_power_factor -> lc_oscillations -> transformer). This sim teaches the POWER consequence of the series-LCR circuit: instantaneous power p(t)=v*i as a double-frequency wave riding a non-zero DC offset; that offset

= V_rms*I_rms*cos(phi), the average (real) power; the power factor cos(phi) = R/Z as the fraction of apparent power S=V_rms*I_rms that is real; the wattless quadrature current I_rms*sin(phi) that flows without ever spending a joule; where the real power physically lands (P = I_rms^2*R -- all in the resistor, never the reactive elements); and the power triangle P/Q/S as the settled impedance triangle uniformly scaled by I_rms^2. Impedance, phase angle, and resonance arrive as one-clause SETTLED CALLBACKS from series_lcr_circuit, never re-derived. SCOPE: does not treat free LC energy oscillation with the source removed (deferred to lc_oscillations, which inherits this sim's energy-ledger instrument and its p<0=energy-returned sign convention), does not treat transmission-line voltage step-up or the wattless-current-on-transmission-lines motivation (deferred to transformer; transmission stays narration-only here, via the real-world anchor), and does not use complex power notation (out of syllabus scope). Conceptual-only (no mode_overrides), EPIC-L-first (no epic_c_branches; the two power-factor misconceptions -- 'average AC power is V_rms times I_rms' and 'a bigger AC current always means bigger power' -- are confronted inside EPIC-L via Rule 16a misconception_watch at exactly STATE_4 and STATE_6, each a straightforward wrong-consequence-first contrast beat, never a predict-pause). Routed to the NEW field_3d 'ac_power' scenario (prefix pwr_) -- an ADDITIVE clone-sibling of the sealed ac_series_lcr scenario plus the element scenarios' power machinery (the averaging wattmeter, the p(t) product pane, the per-element energy gauge), built for this concept (engine log Stage 6, commit 9df14e3). Zero edits to any sealed scenario. Handoff FROM series_lcr_circuit: inherits the apparatus (heater/coil/plates docked in one series loop), the five-arrow phasor machinery (reused here as a two-arrow v/i fan with a current-component split), and the impedance triangle with phi as the circuit's own angle -- all one-clause callbacks. Handoff TO lc_oscillations (next): delivers the energy-ledger instrument (per-element E_L=1/2*L*i^2, E_C=1/2*C*v^2 gauges, borrow-and-return convention), the p<0=energy-returned sign convention, and the settled power vocabulary ('an ideal LC loop is ALL wattless -- nothing ever lands') -- withholds the UNDRIVEN circuit, free oscillation at a NATURAL frequency, the q(t)/i(t) SHM analogy, and any damped decay (none of that renders here; every energy gauge runs under the driven source).

real_world_anchor.primary: The electricity grid's least-known enemy. A factory floor of electric motors draws current through kilometres of line. Motors are coils — inductive — so part of every motor's current is wattless: it flows, but delivers zero energy. The wires don't know the difference — they heat by I²R on the FULL current, working and wattless alike. That is why heavy machines carry a power-factor rating, why a poor power factor draws a financial penalty from a large consumer, and why equipment is rated in two numbers at once — the kilowatts actually delivered, and the larger kilovolt-amps the wires must be built to survive. The paradox this sim shows — more current, yet less power — is a grid engineer's daily arithmetic. Culture-neutral (motors and transmission lines exist everywhere) and physics-true at every depth.
real_world_anchor.secondary: A compressor or motor nameplate reading '1.5 kW / 2.1 kVA' is quoting real power, apparent power, and — silently, in the ratio between them — the power factor. Mains frequency, where it matters at all, stays neutral ('the mains frequency'), never a fixed regional number.

f_demo.name: Demo-compressed AC frequency (real mains is tens of Hz)

L.name: Self-inductance of the coil (off-grid default, snap-on-first-drag)

C.name: Capacitance of the plates (off-grid default, snap-on-first-drag)

omega.name: True angular frequency (rad/s) — used only inside closed-form calculus (E_R_t), never for on-screen degree display

omega_deg_per_s.name: Angular speed in deg/s — drives the degree-native rendering clock theta(t)

theta.name: Instantaneous phase, the state's own clock (Rule 26), degree-native. theta0 = 0 in EVERY state.
theta.derived: theta = omega_deg_per_s * t  [t = time since STATE ENTRY, pure closed form, no accumulator]

T.name: Period of one full AC cycle at the currently active f_demo

X.name: Net (signed) reactance — callback from series_lcr_circuit, winner-hue colour (violet X_L wins / green X_C wins)

Z.name: Impedance — callback from series_lcr_circuit, the STATE_8 triangle hypotenuse before its power-triangle morph

im.name: Peak (amplitude) current — the amber reference, callback from series_lcr_circuit

phi.name: Phase angle by which the SOURCE leads the current (positive = current lags = inductive dominant). Settled in series_lcr_circuit; re-used here without re-derivation.

cosphi.name: Power factor — fraction of apparent power that is real. Dual-labeled once at STATE_4 (power factor cos phi), bare thereafter.
cosphi.derived: cosphi = R/Z  [= P/S identically, STATE_4 closure]

sinphi.name: Signed quadrature fraction (never separately named on-canvas; feeds Q and i_perp only)

V_rms.name: RMS source voltage — the DC-equivalent rating, callback from ac_voltage_resistor

I_rms.name: RMS current — displayed at 3dp so the STATE_4/5/7 displayed-addend chips close

v_t.name: Instantaneous SOURCE voltage — strip cyan trace / fan cyan arrow projection

i_t.name: Instantaneous current — strip amber trace / fan amber arrow projection / bead-drive value

p_t.name: Instantaneous TOTAL circuit power p=v*i — SIGNED, can go negative off resonance (L/C returning energy). The literal pointwise product of v_t and i_t at the SAME theta sample — never an independently-computed curve that merely agrees (Rule 32a).

p_R_t.name: Instantaneous power actually DISSIPATED in R alone — ALWAYS >= 0, the correct driver for the heater glow. Distinct from the signed p_t, which includes the L/C borrowed-and-returned share.

P.name: Average (real) power — the wattmeter's steady reading, the STATE_4/7/9 payoff.
P.derived: P = V_rms*I_rms*cosphi = I_rms^2*R  [three equivalent routes, STATE_7 closure]

S.name: Apparent power — the naive volts-times-amps ceiling. Concept and value are CORE, debuting at STATE_4 (needed for the first misconception pivot); only the formal VA-unit power-triangle-leg treatment is extended, confined to STATE_8.

Q.name: Reactive power. Dual-labeled 'reactive power Q (VAR)' at first mention (STATE_8), NEVER 'Q factor' — this concept declares no f0/delta_f/sharpness-Q variable anywhere; that symbol belongs to series_lcr_circuit only.

i_par.name: In-phase (power-hue) current component — the shadow that does work, STATE_5 primary aha

i_perp.name: Quadrature (wattless) current component — dual-labeled once at STATE_5/6 as 'wattless (idle) current'

V_C_t.name: Instantaneous capacitor voltage — callback formula from series_lcr_circuit (lags i by 90deg), feeds E_C_t only

E_L_t.name: Instantaneous inductor energy — breathes 0..E_L_peak, net zero per cycle (STATE_7)

E_L_peak.name: Peak inductor energy at the current im

E_C_t.name: Instantaneous capacitor energy — breathes 0..E_C_peak, net zero per cycle, OPPOSITE phase from E_L_t (quadrature energy exchange)

E_R_t.name: Cumulative energy dissipated in R since STATE ENTRY (Rule 26 state-local clock) — closed-form integral of i(t)^2*R dt, never an accumulator. Monotone non-decreasing by construction.
E_R_t.derived: E_R_t = P*t - (P/(2*omega))*sin(2*omega*t)   [t in s, sin argument in TRUE radians via omega=2*PI*f_demo]

bead_frac.name: Bead position along the shared loop path (heater-coil-plates, ONE stream, never splits/pools) — callback pattern from series_lcr_circuit

A_frac.name: Bead-excursion visual scale, calibrated to 0.30 at defaults

P_REF_R.name: FIXED heater-glow reference (never self-normalized per-frame) — equals both vm*im and R*im^2 at resonance defaults (20.0 W)

f_glide_deltaT.name: STATE_3 f-glide schedule duration (0.25 to 0.50 Hz)

R_cycle_down_deltaT.name: STATE_6 R-cycle leg A duration (5.0 to 2.0 Ohm)

R_cycle_hold_deltaT.name: STATE_6 R-cycle paradox-hold beat at R=2.0 Ohm — deliberately long so the settled/paused frame (and THE EYE's 60s-clamped reveal pin) lands inside the hold, never the auto-revert leg back to 5.0 Ohm

R_cycle_up_deltaT.name: STATE_6 R-cycle leg A-prime duration (2.0 to 5.0 Ohm, EASED — never an instant snap)

formulas.reference_convention: i(t)=im sin(theta) is the 0-phase reference; v(t)=vm sin(theta+phi) is the SOURCE, offset +phi ahead — inherited verbatim from series_lcr_circuit's resolved convention
formulas.instantaneous_power: p(t)=v(t)*i(t) — the literal pointwise product, sample-for-sample with the strip's own v/i traces (STATE_2/3)
formulas.resistor_power: p_R(t)=i(t)^2*R >= 0 always — the ONLY power that ever actually lands (STATE_7); distinct from the SIGNED total p(t)=v*i which includes the L/C borrowed-and-returned share
formulas.apparent_power: S = V_rms*I_rms (STATE_4, CORE — the volts-times-amps ceiling)
formulas.power_factor: cosphi = R/Z = P/S (STATE_4 callback to the delivered impedance triangle)
formulas.reactive_power: Q = V_rms*I_rms*sinphi = I_rms^2*X (STATE_8, EXTENDED — dual-label 'reactive power Q (VAR)' once, never 'Q factor')
formulas.current_components: i_par = I_rms*cosphi (power-hue, along v); i_perp = I_rms*sinphi (wattless, perpendicular to v); the vector sum i_par + i_perp = i (STATE_5)
formulas.energy_ledger: E_L(t)=0.5*L*i(t)^2, E_C(t)=0.5*C*v_C(t)^2 both breathe (net zero per cycle, opposite phase); E_R(t)=P*t-(P/(2*omega))*sin(2*omega*t) ratchets monotonically (STATE_7)
formulas.power_triangle: P=I_rms^2*R, Q=I_rms^2*X, S=I_rms^2*Z — literally the impedance triangle (R,X,Z) uniformly scaled by I_rms^2, right angle preserved (STATE_8)
formulas.derivation_chain: p(t) = i(t)*v(t) = im*vm*sin(theta)*sin(theta+phi) = (vm*im/2)*[cos(phi) - cos(2*theta+phi)] -> average = (vm*im/2)*cos(phi) = V_rms*I_rms*cos(phi) (STATE_9)

constraints: P = I_rms^2*R = V_rms*I_rms*cosphi at every steady state — three routes, one number.
S = V_rms*I_rms is the CEILING; P <= S always, with equality only at cosphi=1 (unity power factor, resonance in this build).
Q is never lost energy — it is borrowed and returned by L and C every cycle (net zero) — but the wires still carry the current that creates it.
cosphi = R/Z is bounded in [0,1] for any R>0, Z>=R>0 — never negative, never exceeds 1.
S^2 = P^2 + Q^2 is exact in TRUE (unrounded) values — the displayed 2dp addends do NOT close this identity; never render it as a chippable arithmetic equation.
p_R(t) = i(t)^2*R is never negative — the resistor never returns energy; only the TOTAL p(t)=v*i (which includes the L/C exchange) goes negative off resonance.

aha_moment.statement: Only the current's in-phase shadow does work — the rest flows forever, spending nothing.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: The amber current arrow splits into two dashed components; only the one aligned with the voltage reproduces the meter's 3.08 W.

exit_pills.foundational_to_wattless: So where do the other 0.653 amps go? →

STATE_1.title: The wattmeter reads ten — volts times amps seems to work

scene_composition.text: Same as the bare heater's own value — park that

tts_sentences.text_en: A wattmeter docks onto our familiar heater, coil, and capacitor loop.
Watch the needle climb, then settle right at ten watts.
Seven oh seven volts times one point four one four amps gives that number exactly.
A bare heater alone dissipates exactly this much; a lone coil dissipates none. Does volts times amps always work?

STATE_2.title: Power is the instant product — a double-frequency wave

scene_composition.text: p(t) = v(t) · i(t) — a double-frequency wave
Average sits exactly on the needle — 10.0 W

tts_sentences.text_en: Beneath the loop, a matching pair of graphs appears: voltage and current, in step.
A cursor walks one full cycle, multiplying voltage and current together at every instant.
The result is a new wave at double the frequency, touching zero, never dipping below.
Its average sits exactly on the needle: ten watts, the same number.

STATE_3.title: Off the home frequency, part of every cycle flows backward

scene_composition.text: Part of every cycle now flows back

tts_sentences.text_en: Slide the frequency away from home, and watch the beads slow down.
The current's crest visibly drifts late behind the voltage's: something in this loop pushes back.
Watch the wave beneath sink below zero; part of every cycle now flows backward.
The average slides from ten watts down toward three watts. Try the frequency yourself.

STATE_4.title: Volts times amps is only apparent power

scene_composition.text: cos φ = R/Z = 0.555 — the power factor

tts_sentences.text_en: Volts times amps predicts five point five five watts.
The real needle holds at three point zero eight — that guess is struck out.
Divide the two and you get zero point five five five.
That's the circuit's own angle, cosine phi, the power factor — only that fraction survives as real power.

misconception_watch.belief: Average AC power is simply V_rms times I_rms — the volts-times-amps product.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: A ghost needle swings to the naive 5.55 W prediction while the real needle holds at 3.08 W; the struck chip '7.07 × 0.785 = 5.55 W?' sits beside the unmoving real reading.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Volts times amps is only the apparent power — the ceiling; the real power is that times cos φ, the fraction that survives the circuit's own angle.

STATE_5.title: Only the in-phase shadow of the current does work

scene_composition.text: I_rms cos φ = 0.435 A — does the work
I_rms sin φ = 0.653 A — spends nothing

tts_sentences.text_en: Freeze the spinning current arrow, fifty six degrees behind the voltage.
It splits into two: one part lined up with the voltage, doing all the work.
The other part sits perpendicular; it flows, but spends nothing at all.
Seven oh seven volts times that one working shadow gives three point zero eight watts again.

STATE_6.title: More current, fewer watts — the wattless current

tts_sentences.text_en: Watch resistance drop from five ohms to two; the beads speed up.
Current climbs to point nine one one amps.
Yet the needle falls to one point six six watts.
Here reactance dominates: at the home frequency, dropping resistance does the opposite.
These extra amps are wattless; they flow, but never spend a joule.

misconception_watch.belief: A bigger AC current always means bigger power consumption.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: Resistance steps from 5.0 to 2.0 Ω: the current visibly climbs from 0.785 to 0.911 A while the wattmeter needle FALLS from 3.08 to 1.66 W, and the fan's perpendicular component visibly fattens.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Only the in-phase part of the current does work — the extra amps are wattless: they shuttle energy back and forth without ever spending it.

STATE_7.title: All the real power lands in the heater

scene_composition.text: E_L, E_C breathe — net zero every cycle
E_R climbs +6.15 J every cycle, alone

tts_sentences.text_en: Three energy gauges dock: coil, plates, and heater, side by side.
Coil and plates exchange energy each cycle; net zero, stored and returned.
Only the heater climbs; six point one five joules, every cycle, never giving any back.
That's three point zero eight watts again, the meter's number, a third way.

STATE_8.title: The impedance triangle becomes the power triangle

tts_sentences.text_en: The impedance triangle detaches; watch it rescale from ohms into watts.
Its three legs relabel: three oh eight watts real, four six two reactive, five five five apparent.
The reactive power isn't lost; it's stored and returned, but the wires still carry it.
At the home frequency, not shown here, this triangle would flatten completely.

STATE_9.title: The average power, derived from first principles

tts_sentences.text_en: Power is current times voltage, written out fully.
A product to sum identity splits that into a constant plus a wiggle.
That wiggle term averages to zero over a full cycle.
What survives is rms voltage times rms current times cosine phi.
Plug in our numbers, and it lands at three point zero eight watts.

STATE_10.title: Explore — the whole power story, live

scene_composition.text: Drag f, R, L, C, v_m — watch it all move

tts_sentences.text_en: Explore it yourself — drag peak voltage, frequency, resistance, inductance, and capacitance, and watch the whole power story move together.

assessment.mastery_definition: A student has mastered AC power and the power factor when they can (1) explain that instantaneous power p(t)=v·i oscillates at double the source frequency around a non-zero average, and that an averaging wattmeter reads that average, not the swinging instant; (2) compute average power as P=V_rms·I_rms·cos φ and explain why this is always at most the apparent power V_rms·I_rms, with equality only at unity power factor; (3) explain the power factor cos φ = R/Z as the fraction of the current in phase with the voltage, and identify the wattless (out-of-phase) component I_rms sin φ that flows without delivering energy; (4) explain why a rising current does not always mean rising power, since a growing wattless share can make current and power move in opposite directions; (5) state that in a series LCR circuit all real power lands in the resistor alone (P=I_rms²R), while the inductor and capacitor only borrow and fully return energy each cycle; and (6) read the power triangle (P, Q, S) as the impedance triangle scaled by I_rms², with cos φ = P/S.

questions.stem: In an AC circuit, a wattmeter's needle stays steady while the instant-by-instant power visibly swings up and down as you watch the product wave. What is actually happening?

options.A: The instantaneous power p(t)=v(t)i(t) genuinely oscillates at TWICE the source frequency about a steady, non-zero average — the needle reads that average, not the swinging instant value
options.B: The oscillation happens at the same frequency as the source voltage, not double it
options.C: The wattmeter must be broken, since a true power reading should never swing
options.D: Power only ever equals the average value — it never actually swings instant to instant

distractor_misconceptions.B: Squaring or multiplying a sine by itself doubles the frequency (sin²ωt ~ cos2ωt) — it's easy to assume the product wave simply mirrors the source's own frequency
distractor_misconceptions.C: This treats a physically real double-frequency oscillation as an instrument fault rather than the true instantaneous behaviour
distractor_misconceptions.D: This denies that p(t)=v·i is a genuine time-varying quantity — the meter's steady reading is only the cycle average, not the instant-by-instant truth

questions.tested_idea: Instantaneous power p(t)=v·i genuinely oscillates at double the source frequency about a non-zero average; a wattmeter reads that average, not the swinging instant.
questions.parallel_form_stem: If you doubled the source frequency, would the product wave's own oscillation frequency also double?

questions.stem: A circuit's rms voltage is 7.07 V and its rms current is 0.785 A. A wattmeter, however, reads only 3.08 W. What explains the gap?

options.A: The average power is V_rms·I_rms·cos φ, not V_rms·I_rms alone — only the fraction of current in phase with the voltage, set by the power factor cos φ, delivers real power
options.B: 7.07 × 0.785 = 5.55 W is the true average power; the wattmeter itself is reading incorrectly
options.C: Some of the power is lost as heat somewhere else in the circuit before reaching the meter
options.D: The rms values themselves must be wrong if they don't multiply to the meter's reading

distractor_misconceptions.B: This is the confronted misconception — volts times amps is only the APPARENT power, the ceiling, not the delivered real power
distractor_misconceptions.C: Nothing is 'lost' — the missing amount is the wattless portion of the current that never did work in the first place, not a heat leak
distractor_misconceptions.D: The rms values are exactly right; it is the multiplication rule itself (real power equals apparent power alone) that fails whenever a phase angle exists

questions.tested_idea: Real (average) power equals apparent power times the power factor cos φ; volts times amps alone over-predicts whenever a phase angle exists.
questions.parallel_form_stem: If the power factor were exactly 1, would the wattmeter's reading equal V_rms times I_rms exactly?

questions.stem: Why does only the current's in-phase component, I_rms cos φ, deliver power, while the perpendicular component I_rms sin φ does not?

options.A: Only the component of current IN PHASE with the voltage (the projection I_rms cos φ) delivers energy; the perpendicular component (I_rms sin φ) flows but is never aligned with the voltage doing work
options.B: The perpendicular component is lost as heat in the coil and capacitor before it can do work
options.C: cos φ is just efficiency — it measures how much of the current's energy the circuit wastes
options.D: The split is arbitrary — any current could be divided this way, it's just a bookkeeping trick with no physical meaning

distractor_misconceptions.B: Nothing is lost as heat in an ideal L or C — the perpendicular current is genuinely wattless, not dissipated, exactly as the energy ledger shows
distractor_misconceptions.C: Efficiency implies energy is consumed and wasted; the perpendicular current is never consumed at all — it is simply out of step with the voltage
distractor_misconceptions.D: The split is a real physical decomposition: only the in-phase projection lines up with the voltage doing work; it isn't an arbitrary choice

questions.tested_idea: Power delivery depends on the phase alignment between voltage and current; only the in-phase current projection (I_rms cos φ) actually does work.
questions.parallel_form_stem: If the phase angle φ were 90°, what would I_rms cos φ equal, and what would that mean for the delivered power?

questions.stem: A circuit's resistance is lowered and the current rises noticeably, yet the wattmeter's reading falls. Is this possible?

options.A: Yes — a large current can carry mostly wattless (out-of-phase) current; lowering R here strengthens the reactance's dominance, so more amps flow while less real power is delivered
options.B: No — more current in a circuit always means more power is being consumed
options.C: No — this can only happen if the wattmeter is broken
options.D: Yes, but only because some current is being lost through leakage before reaching the resistor

distractor_misconceptions.B: This is the confronted misconception — current and power move together only when the power factor stays fixed; when reactance dominates, they can move in OPPOSITE directions
distractor_misconceptions.C: The meter reading is genuinely correct — physically, dropping R here increases the wattless (idle) share of the current, so real power really does fall
distractor_misconceptions.D: There is no leakage in this circuit — every amp of current is real amperage, it is simply mostly wattless (out of phase), not physically vanishing

questions.tested_idea: A rising current does not guarantee rising power — when reactance dominates, more current can be almost entirely wattless, so power can fall even as current rises.
questions.parallel_form_stem: At resonance, where reactance is already zero, would dropping R the same way raise or lower the power — and why is the answer different?

questions.stem: In a series LCR circuit, where does the real (average) power actually get dissipated, and how is it calculated?

options.A: All of it lands in the resistor alone — P = I_rms²·R; the inductor and capacitor only borrow and fully return energy every cycle, dissipating nothing
options.B: It is shared among the resistor, inductor, and capacitor in proportion to their reactances
options.C: It is dissipated equally by all three elements, since they all oppose the current
options.D: It depends only on the source voltage, not on which elements are present

distractor_misconceptions.B: This is the demoted belief that reactive elements 'consume their share' — the energy ledger shows L and C returning every joule they borrow, net zero per cycle
distractor_misconceptions.C: Opposing current (reactance) is not the same as dissipating energy — only a resistor actually converts electrical energy to heat
distractor_misconceptions.D: The power delivered depends on BOTH the source and which elements are present — a different circuit at the same voltage dissipates a different amount

questions.tested_idea: In a series LCR circuit, ALL real power is dissipated in the resistor alone (P=I_rms²R); the inductor and capacitor borrow and fully return energy each cycle, dissipating nothing.
questions.parallel_form_stem: If the resistor were removed entirely (a pure LC loop), what would the average power delivered by the source be, and why?

questions.stem: At this circuit's resonant (home) frequency, a wattmeter reads exactly V_rms times I_rms. What does that tell you about the power factor there?

options.A: The power factor cos φ equals exactly 1 at resonance — impedance collapses to pure resistance, so the current is perfectly in phase with the voltage
options.B: The power factor must be zero at resonance, since resonance is about the reactive elements cancelling
options.C: The power factor cannot be determined from this observation alone
options.D: Resonance has no effect on the power factor — it is set only by the resistor's value

distractor_misconceptions.B: This confuses 'the reactances cancel' with 'the power factor vanishes' — cancelling reactance makes the circuit purely resistive, which gives the MAXIMUM power factor (1), not zero
distractor_misconceptions.C: Watching the wattmeter reading equal V_rms·I_rms exactly IS the signature of cos φ = 1 — apparent power and real power coincide only when the power factor is unity
distractor_misconceptions.D: The power factor depends on the whole circuit's impedance triangle (R, X, Z), and resonance directly sets X to zero, which directly sets cos φ to 1

questions.tested_idea: At resonance, net reactance is zero, impedance equals resistance alone, and the power factor is exactly 1 — apparent and real power coincide.
questions.parallel_form_stem: Off resonance, is the power factor ever exactly 1 again for a different combination of L and C at the same frequency?
